definitions.explanation: A thin stick of wood, bamboo, or metal used for piercing and holding food for grilling or frying. A staple item in Japanese street food and izakaya cuisine.

examples.japanese: {屋台|やたい}で{串焼|くしや}きを{三本|さんぼん}{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought three skewers of grilled food at a street stall.

examples.japanese: {串|くし}カツは{大阪|おおさか}の{名物|めいぶつ}で、{二度漬|にどづ}けは{禁止|きんし}だ。
examples.english: Kushikatsu is an Osaka specialty, and double-dipping the sauce is forbidden.

notes:
A thin stick used for piercing food, central to many Japanese dishes. Skewered foods are a major category in Japanese cuisine, from yakitori to kushikatsu.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {串|くし}に{刺|さ}す — to thread onto a skewer
- {串焼|くしや}き — skewer-grilled food
- {串|くし}カツ — deep-fried skewered cutlets
- {焼|や}き{鳥|とり}の{串|くし} — yakitori skewer
- {串|くし}{団子|だんご} — skewered dango

COUNTING PATTERNS:
Skewered items are counted with {本|ほん} (the counter for long thin objects): {一本|いっぽん}、{二本|にほん}、{三本|さんぼん}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {櫛|くし} — comb (same pronunciation, different kanji and meaning)
- {竹串|たけぐし} — bamboo skewer
- {金串|かなぐし} — metal skewer
